display.purpose: The room code on the hosting panel only (2.75rem, 3.25rem from 640px). Tabular, tracked wide like a platform number.

headline.purpose: The home band's one-sentence promise (2.125rem, 2.5rem from 640px), text-wrap balance.

title.purpose: Screen titles on waiting and ended screens (1.875rem); 'You're connected' on the stage uses 1.75rem to 2rem.

item.purpose: A file stop's name. The band wordmark uses the same weight at 1.3rem, -0.02em.

body.purpose: Explanations and notices, 0.95rem to 1.05rem, capped near 34rem.

label.purpose: Plate details, captions, station names (800), quiet links, buttons (base size, 800).

data.purpose: Every live number: speeds, sizes, durations, ping, lanes, codes. Always tabular-nums.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: The one panel elevation (connect, hosting and ended panels, notices). Light mode.

shadows.name: self-view
shadows.purpose: Your own camera preview in the stage corner.

shadows.name: sheet-backdrop
shadows.purpose: Backdrop behind the modal sheet (background, not a shadow).

shadows.name: focus
shadows.purpose: Focus ring everywhere; outline turns band-ink on the navy band.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Press feedback, progress width, sheet fade, ringing pulse.

motion.name: ease-drawer
motion.purpose: Sheet travel and the train running along the line.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Every pressable answers the press; colours ease over 160ms.

motion.name: sheet
motion.value: opacity 220ms ease-out, transform 260ms ease-drawer; from translateY(12px) scale(0.98), phones from translateY(100%)

motion.name: line-build
motion.purpose: Dashes run while the line is being built (connecting).

motion.name: train
motion.value: 1.6s ease-drawer infinite, fades in and out at 12% and 88%
motion.purpose: A train runs end to end while files move.

motion.name: ringing
motion.purpose: Incoming call pulse in line purple, the only looping motion in a sheet.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation and transition durations 0.01ms, one iteration
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion stops all of the above.

narrative.overview:
The connection is a metro line with exactly two stations. You and Them are the termini, the purple line between them is the path, the ticks under it are the real file lanes, and a train runs along it while files move. Every screen starts with a navy signage band carrying that line and a line-name plate that says how you are connected ("Direct on the same network (IPv4), <1 ms ping, 4 lanes"). Below the band is the platform: a pale tile ground with soft white panels, the dark call stage, and the files column drawn as stops on a vertical purple line.

The world is transit signage, not app chrome. Type is Overpass (a highway-signage face) set heavy, labels are plain sentences, and status colours are lamps that mean exactly one thing each. Density is calm: one panel or one stage plus one column, generous 48px controls, phones and laptops treated equally. Motion is mechanical and purposeful: dashes run while a line is being built, a train runs while files move, a ring pulses while a call is ringing, and everything else is still.

The category default this world refuses is a status pill floating over a generic video tile. Connection truth lives in the band, always, and a relayed line can never look like a direct one.
keyCharacteristics: Navy signage band on every screen holds the wordmark, the metro line and the line-name plate.
Purple is the line: the primary action, the files line, the focus ring, the caret.
Green, amber and red are lamps (direct, relayed, lost) and nothing else.
Overpass Variable, heavy (800) for anything you read first; tabular figures for every number.
8px plates for controls, 14px soft-shadowed panels without borders, full circles for stations and call controls.
Light and dark follow the system; the band stays navy in both.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Green means direct, amber means relayed, red means lost or destructive. Never use a lamp colour for decoration, branding or emphasis.

rules.name: The Band Token Rule
rules.body: Anything on the navy band uses `band-*` tokens; anything on the ground or panels uses the ground tokens. The band values are tuned for navy and are not swapped in dark mode.

rules.name: The Line Is Purple Rule
rules.body: Purple marks the path and the action that moves along it. It is never a status colour: a direct plate is purple with a green lamp, not green.

rules.name: The Tabular Truth Rule
rules.body: Every live number (ping, speed, bytes, time, lane count, code) is set in tabular figures so it never jitters while it updates.

rules.name: The Sentence Label Rule
rules.body: Labels are sentence case, plain words. No uppercase kickers or eyebrows above headings; the only uppercase is the typed room code.

rules.name: The No-Border Panel Rule
rules.body: Panels are separated by the lift and the tile ground, never by a stroke. Rings are reserved for focus, drag-over, the received-file card and the flat plate.

dos: **Do** put the navy band with the metro line and line-name plate at the top of every screen, and keep the connection type visible in it at all times.
**Do** draw new connection or transfer states as states of the line (track style, ticks, interchange, break, train) before reaching for a badge.
**Do** use `band-*` tokens on the band and ground tokens below it.
**Do** set every changing number in tabular figures.
**Do** give anything pressable the press response (scale 0.97, 160ms) and the 3px purple focus outline.
**Do** use the flat plate when status sits next to a primary button.
**Do** keep one primary (purple) button per view; the stage gets the white stage button instead.
donts: **Don't** use green, amber or red for anything but direct, relayed and lost or destructive states.
**Don't** let a relayed connection share the direct plate's purple; relayed is always amber with the "Relay" interchange on the line.
**Don't** put borders on panels or add a second panel shadow; use the Lift.
**Don't** float a status pill over the video; status belongs to the band.
**Don't** add uppercase eyebrows or kickers above headings.
**Don't** animate anything that is not a real process (building the line, files moving, a call ringing); reduced motion stops all of it.
